anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions compete for incompatible locks on the same data or metadata objects, causing queues, blocking chains, or deadlocks that throttle throughput and force rollbacks.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level settings for memory, logging, checkpoints, parallelism, or connection limits are mis-tuned for the hardware or workload, so internal subsystems stall or thrash despite no real shortage of physical resources.

When both root causes strike together, the system exhibits lock wait times and deadlock rates that rise erratically in tandem with configuration-induced stalls. Symptoms include long-lasting blocker–waiter trees that suddenly cascade after checkpoints, deadlock storms following aggressive lock-escalation, CPU cores oscillating between idle and spin while sessions are stuck on lock waits, transaction-throughput saw-toothing as mis-sized log buffers force frequent flushes that hold critical locks, and application timeouts escalating even though raw hardware utilization appears modest.

The causal chain is mutually reinforcing: sub-optimal parameters (e.g., too small buffer pool, undersized log or overly frequent checkpoints, inflated work-mem driving spill and lock-escalation) lengthen statement execution and keep transactions open longer, enlarging their lock footprint and probability of collision. Simultaneously, heavy blocking stretches transaction lifetimes, inflating in-memory structures and redo volume, which magnifies the impact of any memory, logging, or background-worker misconfiguration. Each feedback loop intensifies the other, pushing the database into a state where locks and mis-tuned internals alternately throttle progress and obscure each other's contribution, complicating diagnosis and recovery.

entry.official_definition: Maximum wait for connection, in seconds; zero or not specified means wait indefinitely.
entry.trigger_condition: A libpq client connection attempt exceeds connect_timeout seconds.
entry.workload_impact: The client connection attempt fails instead of waiting indefinitely.
entry.default_behavior: Zero or absent value means wait indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
